new_statements.quote: Like Bantu languages, Bә̀mbәlә̀ is a tone language- Tones are of great importance in the study of tonal languages like Bә̀mbәlә̀- Most often, if not always, they play a distinctive function in those languages. [...] Four tones are identified in Bә̀mbәlә̀. They are high ( ́ ), low ( ̀ ), Low high ( ̌ ) and High-low ( ̂ ). [...] The four tones indentified as tonetic are also tonemic. (sec. 2.2.3-2.2.3.2, print pp. 56-57 = pdf pp. 79-80) / Conclusion 2.4, print p. 60: 'we have identified 45 consonant phonemes, 15 vowel phonemes and 4 tonemes.'

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record. First opened description of Bebele phonology: tone language, 4 tonemes, no word-stress statement. Compatible with the LINCOM 2014 grammar blurb held by the project ('sound system and tone patterns').
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bә̀mbәlә̀ is described as a tone language with four tonemes (H, L and contour LH, HL; the general conclusion restates 2 level + 2 contour tones). The phonology chapter (segments, tones, syllable structure V/CV/CVC) contains no section or statement on word stress/accent; the only occurrence of 'stress' in the thesis (print p. 303, orthography chapter) is a generic textbook definition of the phonological word ('each phonological word normally only contains a single primary stress or only one tone'), not a claim about Bә̀mbәlә̀ stress placement. Intonation is mentioned only for polar questions (rising final intonation) and topic/focus.
new_statements.identity_note: Bә̀mbәlә̀ (Bebele, ISO beb, Glottolog bebe1248), Bantu A70 (Guthrie; CODESRIA abstract says A40) spoken in Haute-Sanaga (Minta, Bibey, Nsem), Centre Region, Cameroon; the thesis describes the language as a whole with an orthography standardised across its dialects via the 'total immersion approach'.
